column1: # Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines that start with # are ignored. Every
# field must hold text. Two row kinds:
#       Keeps known findings out of the failing count. <needle> is a fixed
#       string searched in the printed finding text (message plus
#       "(section: <heading>)"). <count> is the exact number of findings the
#       row covers: a fixed defect (fewer) or a new one (more) fails the run,
#       so a row cannot rot or hide a second defect. <backlog-slug> names the
#       local backlog item that owns the fix. Each row is printed on every run.
#       Says that <suite> (a test.sh, test-*.sh or *-test.sh) runs the bash
#       fences under the first heading of <file> that holds <heading-needle>.
#       `check` proves the heading still holds a bash fence and that the suite
#       names the heading; `run` runs each suite once from the repo root.

column7: The Step 1b fence defines the helper; Steps 2d, 3c, 6a and 6h call it from fresh shells, so the call fails. Not a WP 2-01 member. CDT-324 (WP 2-10, wp-2-10-retro-scheduled) owns the fix.
